newsitem.title: USA: Pilot union spokesman sees glimmers of hope.
newsitem.headline: Pilot union spokesman sees glimmers of hope.

text.p: A spokesman for the Allied Pilots Association said on Friday there were some signs of progress in talks with American Airlines aimed at averting a strike at midnight (0500 GMT Saturday).
The union's communications director, David Bates, said there were "some glimmers of hope" in discussions with the airline. He declined to give any details.
That hint of optimism contrasted with comments earlier in the day by union president James Sovich who described the negotiations as "slow and difficult."
Meanwhile, the union's board has started meeting away from the site of negotiations.
The board was expected to give Sovich the authority to declare a strike if the talks with American fail.

Fort Worth, Texas-based American carries about 20 percent of the nation's air travelers. If the airline shuts down it is expected to strand thousands of passengers and could cost the economy up to $200 million a day.
